stories.title: Emit WhatsApp typing indicator during AI processing delay
stories.description: When Rainbow AI receives a WhatsApp message and begins processing, send a typing indicator (chat presence 'composing') to the sender immediately, then clear it when the reply is sent. Without this, users see dead silence for 2-6 seconds between sending and receiving a reply, causing perceived unresponsiveness and drop-offs.
acceptanceCriteria: On every incoming WhatsApp message, `sendWhatsAppTypingIndicator` is called with `composing` state before pipeline processing begins
Typing indicator is cleared (paused state sent) immediately when the bot reply is dispatched
If processing takes over 20 seconds the indicator is re-sent to prevent WhatsApp's 25-second auto-dismiss
Typing indicator is NOT sent if the message is silently dropped (duplicate, system message, or ignored group message)
Behaviour is configurable per-profile via settings.json `features.typingIndicator: true|false`
technicalNotes: `sendWhatsAppTypingIndicator` already exists in `src/lib/whatsapp/index.ts` — integrate into `src/assistant/message-router.ts` before pipeline dispatch
Baileys API: `sock.sendPresenceUpdate('composing', jid)` and `sock.sendPresenceUpdate('paused', jid)`
Gate behind `delay > 500ms` check to avoid unnecessary presence updates for instant cached replies

stories.title: Baileys circuit breaker: long cooldown after consecutive reconnect failures
stories.description: The current reconnect logic (3 attempts, max 60s delay) is insufficient to prevent WhatsApp account bans caused by rapid connect/disconnect cycling. When the supervisor and Baileys instance both retry simultaneously, hundreds of failed handshakes can trigger abuse detection. A circuit breaker must open after N consecutive failures and enforce a 30-minute cooldown.
acceptanceCriteria: After 5 consecutive connection failures (configurable), the circuit opens and no further reconnection is attempted for 30 minutes
A WARNING-level log is emitted: `[Baileys:id] Circuit breaker OPEN — 5 consecutive failures. Cooling down for 30 min.`
An admin WhatsApp notification is sent when the circuit opens
After the 30-minute cooldown the circuit enters HALF-OPEN, attempts one reconnection, and either closes (success) or reopens with another 30-min cooldown
Circuit state (open/closed/half-open, last-open timestamp, failure count) is exposed on `GET /api/rainbow/status` per instance
technicalNotes: Implement inside `src/lib/whatsapp/instance.ts` `handleDisconnect()` — replace current 3-attempt counter with a circuit-breaker state machine
Separate from `baileys-supervisor.ts` which handles supervisor-level crashes — this is instance-level connection cycling
Use `Date.now()` timestamps rather than a library; no external dependency needed

stories.title: Monitor WhatsApp message template quality and alert on pause/disable
stories.description: When Meta automatically pauses a template due to low quality rating (spam reports, low read rate), the bot silently fails to deliver proactive messages. A webhook listener and admin alert must detect template pauses before they escalate to permanent disable.
acceptanceCriteria: Incoming `message_template_status_update` webhook events are parsed and persisted to a `template_quality_events` DB table with fields: template_name, old_status, new_status, reason, timestamp
When a template status changes to PAUSED or DISABLED, an admin WhatsApp notification is sent within 60 seconds including template name, new status, and pause duration
Admin dashboard shows current status and quality rating for each registered template
A daily summary of template quality ratings is included in the existing daily performance report
Webhook handler returns HTTP 200 within 5 seconds to avoid Meta retry storms
technicalNotes: Meta sends `message_template_status_update` to the registered webhook — add handler to `src/routes/webhooks/index.ts`
This is a Meta Cloud API webhook, not a Baileys event — requires Meta webhook subscription to include `message_template_status_update` field
Distinct from existing phone number quality tracking in `src/lib/phone-quality.ts`

stories.title: PDPA/GDPR data portability endpoint: export all personal data by JID
stories.description: Malaysia's amended PDPA (effective June 2025) grants data subjects the right to request their personal data in a portable, machine-readable format. The existing GDPR erasure endpoint handles deletion, but there is no corresponding data export endpoint. Businesses processing data from over 20,000 contacts are now legally obligated to fulfil portability requests.
acceptanceCriteria: New endpoint `GET /api/rainbow/guests/:jid/data-export` returns all personal data for the JID as structured JSON
Export includes: all messages (content, timestamps, direction), conversation metadata, intent predictions, feedback records, opt-out status, and conversation state
Response includes a `generated_at` ISO timestamp and `retention_policy` summary
Request is logged to `gdpr_audit_log` table with `action: 'data_export'`
Endpoint requires admin authentication (same auth as erasure endpoint)
Response time under 5 seconds for up to 10,000 messages; returns 202 with a job ID for larger datasets
technicalNotes: Mirror the query pattern from `src/routes/admin/gdpr-erasure.ts` but SELECT instead of DELETE
Canonicalize the JID using `canonicalPhoneKey()` before querying — same as erasure endpoint
Use `Content-Disposition: attachment; filename=data-export-{hash}.json` header for download

stories.title: Per-JID inbound message rate limiter to prevent bot abuse
stories.description: A single WhatsApp number can flood the bot with hundreds of messages per minute, exhausting AI provider quotas and degrading service for all users. The existing rate limiter operates at a profile level, not per individual user JID. A sliding-window per-JID limiter should throttle abusive senders with a polite rejection message.
acceptanceCriteria: Each unique sender JID is limited to 10 messages per 60-second sliding window (configurable per profile in settings.json)
When the limit is exceeded, the bot sends one brief reply: 'Too many messages — please wait a moment before sending more.' and drops subsequent messages until the window resets
The throttle reply is sent at most once per window (not once per dropped message)
Rate limit counters are in-memory (not Redis-dependent) with TTL-based cleanup to avoid memory leaks
Admin dashboard shows current throttled JID count and throttle events in the last 24 hours
technicalNotes: Implement as middleware in `src/assistant/message-router.ts` before pipeline dispatch
Use a `Map<string, {count: number, windowStart: number}>` with periodic cleanup (every 5 minutes)
Default limits: 10 msg/60s; configurable `rateLimiting.perUserWindowMs` and `perUserMaxMessages` in settings.json
Distinct from `src/lib/frequency-cap.ts` (outbound cap) — this is inbound abuse prevention

stories.title: Outbound media pre-send validation against WhatsApp size and format limits
stories.description: When staff or automated workflows send media via `sendWhatsAppMedia`, there is no pre-send validation. Sending an oversized video (>16MB) or unsupported MIME type silently fails at the WhatsApp level with no actionable error surfaced to the admin.
acceptanceCriteria: Before sending, validate MIME type against WhatsApp-supported list: JPEG/PNG (images ≤5MB), MP4 (video ≤16MB, H.264+AAC only), AAC/MP3/OGG/AMR (audio ≤16MB), PDF/DOCX/XLSX (documents ≤100MB)
If validation fails, `sendWhatsAppMedia` throws a structured error with fields: `code: 'MEDIA_VALIDATION_FAILED'`, `reason`, `actualSizeMb`, `limitMb`
Admin API routes that call `sendWhatsAppMedia` return HTTP 422 with the validation error details
A unit test covers each unsupported type and the boundary size condition for images and videos
Validation is skipped when the media URL is a remote HTTPS URL (size cannot be pre-checked without fetching)
technicalNotes: `sendWhatsAppMedia` is in `src/lib/whatsapp/index.ts` — add a `validateMedia(buffer, mimeType)` helper called before `sock.sendMessage()`
WhatsApp size limits: image 5MB, video 16MB, audio 16MB, document 100MB, sticker 100KB
Add `src/lib/whatsapp/media-validator.ts` as a new file with exported `validateWhatsAppMedia()` function

stories.title: CSP connect-src whitelist for AI provider endpoints used by admin dashboard
stories.description: The current Helmet CSP sets `connect-src: ['self']`, which blocks the admin dashboard from making direct API calls to external services (e.g. health-checking AI provider endpoints, loading avatar URLs from WhatsApp CDN). Browser console errors accumulate silently and certain admin features fail without clear diagnostics.
acceptanceCriteria: `connect-src` directive is extended to include: `https://*.nvidia.com`, `https://api.openrouter.ai`, `https://pps.whatsapp.net` (avatar CDN), and any additional AI provider base URLs read from `settings.json`
The CSP report endpoint at `/csp-report` continues to capture violations and logs them at WARN level
A Vitest test verifies that the CSP header string contains the required connect-src values in production mode
No `unsafe-eval` or `unsafe-inline` directives are introduced
`img-src` is extended to include `https://pps.whatsapp.net data:` to allow WhatsApp avatar images in the dashboard
technicalNotes: Edit the `helmet()` call in `src/index.ts` — add to `connectSrc` array
AI provider base URLs can be derived from `src/assistant/data/settings.json` `providers[].baseUrl` at startup
Use `Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only` in development mode to catch violations without blocking

stories.title: Human handoff SLA timer with breach alert to admin
stories.description: When a conversation is escalated to human handoff, there is no mechanism to alert admin if no human responds within an SLA window. Customers left waiting after escalation have significantly higher churn rates than those who never reached a bot.
acceptanceCriteria: When an escalation event is created, a timer starts with configurable SLA duration (default: 15 minutes, configurable per profile as `handoff.slaDurationMinutes`)
If no outbound message is sent on the escalated conversation within the SLA window, an admin WhatsApp alert fires: 'SLA breach: [phone] has been waiting X minutes since escalation at [time]'
The alert includes the last user message for context
If a human replies before the SLA expires, the timer is cancelled and no alert is sent
SLA timer state is persisted to DB so it survives server restarts
Admin dashboard shows open handoffs with elapsed time and SLA status (green/amber/red)
technicalNotes: Integrate with `src/assistant/escalation.ts` — on escalation creation, insert a pending SLA record
Use a cron job (every 2 minutes) to check for breached SLAs rather than Node.js `setTimeout` (which doesn't survive restarts)
`escalation_events` table already exists — add `sla_breached_at` and `human_responded_at` columns via Drizzle migration
Detect human response by checking if an outbound message for that phone was sent after the escalation timestamp

stories.title: System prompt A/B experiment framework for intent response quality
stories.description: The AI system prompt is a single static configuration with no mechanism to test variants. Minor wording changes can produce 5-15% improvements in task completion rate, but there is currently no way to measure that. An experiment framework allows operators to define two prompt variants, split live traffic, and measure resolution rate and fallback rate per variant.
acceptanceCriteria: A new config section `experiments[].id, variants[].weight, variants[].systemPromptOverride` in settings.json is parsed and validated via Zod schema
Traffic is split by deterministic hash of the sender JID modulo total weight, ensuring the same user always gets the same variant within an experiment
Per-variant metrics (message count, fallback rate, CSAT score) are tracked in a new `experiment_metrics` DB table
Admin API `GET /api/rainbow/experiments/:id/results` returns variant comparison with confidence intervals
Experiments can be activated and deactivated without server restart via admin dashboard
When no experiment is active, system falls back to the default system prompt with zero overhead
technicalNotes: Add experiment resolution at the prompt-assembly step in the AI provider manager
Use `crypto.createHash('md5').update(phone + experimentId).digest('hex')` for deterministic assignment
Schema: `experiment_metrics(experiment_id, variant_id, phone_hash, message_count, fallback_count, csat_sum, window_date)`

stories.title: Configurable data retention policy per-profile with admin UI controls
stories.description: Data retention is currently hardcoded globally. Malaysia's PDPA Retention Principle requires retention periods to be set only as long as necessary for the stated purpose, and different profiles (hostel, cafe) have different legal and operational needs.
acceptanceCriteria: Admin UI settings tab shows current retention configuration per profile: `retention_days`, `grace_period_days`, `enabled` toggle
Operators can edit and save retention settings via the existing settings API without requiring a server restart
Preview pane shows count of records that would be soft-deleted and hard-deleted if purge ran now
Settings are validated: `retention_days` must be 30-3650, `grace_period_days` must be 7-365
When retention is disabled for a profile, an audit log entry is created recording who disabled it and when
technicalNotes: `src/lib/data-retention.ts` already reads from `configStore` per profile — the backend logic is complete
Missing piece: admin UI tab + API endpoint to write `settings.retention.*` values back via `configStore.updateSettings()`
Expose `GET /api/rainbow/retention/stats?profile=X` (wrapping `getRetentionStats`) for the preview feature

stories.title: PDPA data breach notification workflow with 72-hour commissioner deadline
stories.description: Malaysia's amended PDPA (Phase 3, June 2025) mandates that data controllers notify the Personal Data Protection Commissioner within 72 hours of discovering a qualifying breach, and notify affected data subjects within 7 days. Rainbow AI stores WhatsApp message history and guest personal data, requiring a documented breach response workflow.
acceptanceCriteria: A new admin endpoint `POST /api/rainbow/security/breach-report` accepts a breach description and creates a timestamped breach record in a `pdpa_breach_log` table
On creation, the system automatically calculates and stores the 72-hour commissioner notification deadline and 7-day subject notification deadline
Admin WhatsApp notification is sent to the system admin with breach details and both deadlines
Admin dashboard shows open breach records with countdown timers to each deadline, colour-coded (green/amber/red)
Breach log is append-only; contains: reported_by, description, affected_count_estimate, commissioner_notified_at (nullable), subjects_notified_at (nullable)
A daily cron job checks for overdue notifications and sends a reminder alert if deadlines are approaching within 6 hours
technicalNotes: Lightweight workflow management — no external PDPC API integration required (notification is done manually by admin, system tracks deadlines)
Create `src/routes/admin/breach-report.ts` following the same pattern as `src/routes/admin/gdpr-erasure.ts`
Use existing `admin-notifier.ts` for the WhatsApp alert

stories.title: WhatsApp media message acknowledgement in AI conversation flow
stories.description: Guests frequently send images (booking confirmations, screenshots, receipts) and voice notes to the hostel WhatsApp. Rainbow AI currently only processes text messages and silently ignores media. Acknowledging media receipt with a context-aware response prevents users from thinking their message was lost.
acceptanceCriteria: Incoming image messages trigger a configurable static reply from the `media_received` static reply key
Incoming audio/voice messages trigger a separate static reply from the `audio_received` key
Incoming document messages trigger a `document_received` reply
Media messages are logged to `rainbow_messages` with `messageType: 'image'|'audio'|'document'` and `mediaUrl` (if available)
The feature is configurable per-profile: `features.mediaRepliesEnabled: true|false` in settings.json
Media replies do not count against conversation fallback rate metrics
technicalNotes: Add media type detection in `src/assistant/pipeline/input-validator.ts` based on `IncomingMessage.messageType`
The `messageType` field already exists on `IncomingMessage` in `src/assistant/types.ts`
Route media messages to a dedicated `media-handler` stage that short-circuits the full NLP pipeline

stories.title: Webchat widget consent banner with timestamped opt-in log
stories.description: The webchat widget collects and processes personal data (chat content) without presenting a data processing consent notice. GDPR and Malaysia's PDPA both require explicit informed consent before initiating data collection. Industry audits find 47% of chatbots lack this, representing a compliance vulnerability.
acceptanceCriteria: On first widget load, a consent banner is shown before the chat interface with [Accept] and [Decline] options
If the user declines, the chat interface is not rendered and a privacy policy link is shown
If the user accepts, the acceptance is stored in `localStorage` with timestamp and not shown again for 365 days
The consent timestamp and a truncated session ID are sent to `POST /api/webchat/consent-log` and persisted to DB
The consent banner is keyboard-accessible and meets WCAG 2.1 AA
Consent text content is configurable per profile via admin settings
technicalNotes: Add consent check at the top of `src/public/js/modules/chat-send.js` before any message is sent
Consent log table: `webchat_consent_log(session_id_hash, accepted_at, profile_id, user_agent_hash)`
Use `localStorage.setItem('rb_consent', JSON.stringify({accepted: true, ts: Date.now()}))` for persistence

stories.title: Baileys DB auth state health check and corruption recovery at startup
stories.description: Baileys session credentials stored in PostgreSQL can become corrupted during a crash mid-transaction. The next reconnection attempt will silently fail with a malformed session error, requiring manual DB intervention. An automatic health check at startup should detect and clear corrupted auth state before attempting connection.
acceptanceCriteria: At server startup, before calling `makeWASocket`, a `validateAuthState(instanceId)` check queries DB auth rows and verifies JSON parseability of credential fields
If validation fails (unparseable JSON, missing required creds fields), corrupted rows are deleted and the QR pairing flow is re-initiated
An admin WhatsApp notification is sent: '[instanceId] auth state was corrupted and cleared — please re-scan QR code'
Validation results are logged at INFO level: `[DbAuth:pelangi] Auth state healthy: creds OK, 42 signal keys`
A new admin endpoint `GET /api/rainbow/instances/:id/auth-health` returns auth state validity without triggering recovery
technicalNotes: Add `validateAuthState(instanceId: string)` to `src/lib/whatsapp/db-auth-state.ts`
Check: `SELECT key, value FROM wa_auth_state WHERE instance_id = $1` — attempt `JSON.parse(value)` for each row
Required credential fields for a valid Baileys session: `noiseKey`, `signedIdentityKey`, `registrationId`, `advSecretKey`
Call validation from `WhatsAppInstance.start()` before `useDbAuthState()` in `src/lib/whatsapp/instance.ts`

stories.title: Structured data notice sent to user on first WhatsApp interaction
stories.description: When a guest initiates their first WhatsApp conversation with the bot, they receive no notification that their messages will be stored and processed. PDPA's Notice and Choice Principle requires data subjects to be informed of collection purposes at or before collection.
acceptanceCriteria: On the very first message from a new JID (no prior `rainbow_conversations` record), a data notice follows the normal welcome response
Notice text is configurable in `knowledge.json` under key `data_notice_first_contact`
The notice is sent only once per JID — subsequent conversations do not include it
If the JID has previously opted out (exists in `opt_outs` table), the notice is not sent
technicalNotes: Check for first-contact in `src/assistant/message-router.ts` using `conversationDb.getOrCreateConversation()` return value — if `created: true`, it is a first contact
Inject the notice as a suffix to the reply before `sendWhatsAppMessage` is called
Reuse existing STOP keyword opt-out handling — do not duplicate opt-out logic

stories.title: Webhook HMAC signature validation for incoming Meta Cloud API events
stories.description: Meta's WhatsApp Cloud API signs incoming webhook payloads with HMAC-SHA256 using the app secret. Without signature validation, the webhook endpoint accepts any HTTP POST, allowing malicious actors to inject fake template status updates, quality rating changes, or delivery receipts. The raw body capture is already in place.
acceptanceCriteria: All requests to `POST /webhooks/meta` are rejected with HTTP 403 if the `X-Hub-Signature-256` header is absent or invalid
Validation computes `hmac-sha256(APP_SECRET, rawBody)` and compares with the header value using constant-time comparison
When validation fails, the rejection is logged at WARN level with the source IP
If `META_APP_SECRET` environment variable is not set, validation is skipped with a startup WARNING log
A unit test covers: valid signature passes, tampered body fails, missing header fails
technicalNotes: `req.rawBody` is already captured in `src/index.ts` via `captureRawBody` middleware
Add `validateMetaSignature(req)` middleware to `src/routes/webhooks/index.ts`
Use `crypto.timingSafeEqual()` for constant-time comparison to prevent timing attacks
Header format: `X-Hub-Signature-256: sha256=<hex-digest>`

stories.title: Update WhatsApp cost tracker for per-message pricing model (July 2025)
stories.description: Meta is transitioning WhatsApp Business from per-conversation to per-message pricing effective July 1, 2025. The existing cost tracking module was built for the conversation-based model. Without updating it, cost estimates in the admin dashboard will be inaccurate by up to 10x for profiles that send many short proactive messages.
acceptanceCriteria: A settings toggle `billing.pricingModel: 'per_conversation' | 'per_message'` is added to settings.json with per-profile support
When `per_message` is active, each outbound message increments a per-message cost counter using configurable per-category rates (marketing, utility, authentication)
The admin dashboard cost chart displays estimated costs under both models with a visual indicator of which model is active
Unit tests cover cost calculation for both pricing models using sample message sequences
technicalNotes: Locate existing cost tracking in `src/routes/admin/whatsapp-cost.ts` and `src/assistant/__tests__/whatsapp-cost.test.ts`
Per-message rates (2025): marketing ~$0.0588, utility ~$0.02 per message — use MYR rates for Malaysia
The message category (marketing/utility) must be determined at send time — proactive messages are typically marketing, reactive replies are utility

stories.title: Webchat widget offline hours banner with configurable business hours
stories.description: The webchat widget is always-open with no indication of business operating hours. When staff are unavailable (late night, public holidays), users send messages expecting prompt responses and become frustrated when none arrives. An unavailability banner set by configurable business hours improves user expectations.
acceptanceCriteria: Business hours are configurable per-profile in admin settings: `businessHours.timezone`, `businessHours.schedule` (array of day/open/close)
When current time is outside business hours, the webchat widget header shows a banner: 'We're currently offline. Leave a message and we'll reply during business hours.'
The input field remains functional (messages can still be sent and will be answered by AI or queued for human review)
Business hours configuration is exposed via `GET /api/webchat/config/:profile` for client-side rendering
Public holiday override can be configured as a list of dates in settings
technicalNotes: Business hours logic should be evaluated server-side in `src/routes/public/webchat-api.ts` and included in the initial widget config payload
Use the `luxon` library (or native `Intl.DateTimeFormat`) for timezone-aware time comparison
The widget config endpoint should return `isAvailable: boolean, nextOpenTime: string | null`

stories.title: Admin audit log for configuration changes with before/after diff
stories.description: Any admin can modify AI system prompts, routing rules, and intent configurations with no record of who changed what and when. When the bot starts behaving unexpectedly after a config change, operators cannot determine root cause. PDPA's Data Integrity Principle also requires that processing decisions be accountable.
acceptanceCriteria: Every write operation through the config API (`PUT /api/rainbow/config/*`, settings updates) inserts a record into `rainbow_config_audit` with: admin_user, endpoint, before (JSON), after (JSON), timestamp
Admin dashboard shows an audit log tab with the last 100 config change events, filterable by date range and admin user
Each audit entry shows a human-readable diff (changed keys highlighted)
Audit records are retained for 365 days (not subject to standard conversation retention policy)
Verify `rainbow_config_audit` table is being populated by ALL config write paths, not just current partial coverage
technicalNotes: `rainbow_config_audit` table already exists — audit routes in `src/routes/admin/config.ts` to identify which write paths are missing
Add an `auditConfigChange(adminUser, endpoint, before, after)` helper and call it from all config mutation routes
The before-value must be captured BEFORE the write — common bug to avoid
